name: Björk
hook: An Icelandic punk singer who moved to London, called house the only truly modern pop music, and made her solo records with the producers of British club music.

blurb.age13: Björk was born in Reykjavík, Iceland, in 1965 and made her first record there as a child. In the 1980s she was the singer of the Sugarcubes, an Icelandic band that became known around the world. When they stopped in 1992 she moved to London and went solo. She said house music was the only really modern pop music being made, and she chose producers from British dance music: Nellee Hooper, who had worked with Soul II Soul and Massive Attack, then Graham Massey of 808 State, Tricky, Howie B, and Mark Bell of the electronic group LFO. Her records mix strings and electronic beats with her very unusual voice. Radiohead named her album 'Homogenic' as one of the influences on 'Kid A'.
blurb.adult: Born in Reykjavík on 21 November 1965, she released an album as a child in 1977 and fronted the Sugarcubes, internationally known by the late 1980s, until they stopped in 1992. 'Debut' (July 1993) was made in London with Nellee Hooper, producer for Soul II Soul and part of the Bristol circle around Massive Attack, and drew on London club culture; she described house music at the time as the only truly modern pop music. 'Post' (1995) brought in Graham Massey of 808 State, Tricky and Howie B, and 'Homogenic' (1997) was built with Mark Bell of LFO, a Warp act, setting string arrangements against harsh programmed beats. Radiohead name 'Homogenic' among the influences on 'Kid A'. 'Fossora' (2022) was the first album she produced entirely alone.
